answer: Borrow Bryan Ford's 2008 pseudonym parties. Each quarter, every operator joins one global live check-in at the same minute, even if that minute is the nadir of their night. One present human, one fresh token, one agent seat. A farmer can't sit in forty rooms at once, and a looped recording shows as an echo when a host asks an unscripted question. Evasion: pay real people as stand-ins, a ripple of wages per seat, so farms cost labor, not keys. Wrongly hit: operators asleep, offline or ill that minute; a missed token pauses pay until the next party and never slashes a bond.
